key_insight: The paper shows that memory retention should be personalized at the fact level, because different users reuse information in different ways. By learning from delayed feedback about what facts are actually retrieved later, the system can make smarter memory-gating decisions than one-size-fits-all policies.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of deciding which facts to keep in a limited long-term memory bank for language-model agents. Existing shared gating policies do not adapt to user-specific patterns of future reuse, so valuable facts may be discarded while less useful ones are retained.
method: Proposes a retrieval-based labeling strategy that marks each fact by whether it is later retrieved and used in responses.
Formulates memory gating as a personalized prediction problem based on delayed one-sided feedback.
Learns fact-level gating policies that better match individual users' future memory needs.
impact: This matters because better memory gating improves personalization, efficiency, and long-term usefulness in LLM agents with limited memory. Practitioners can retain more relevant information while reducing unnecessary memory growth.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of fact extraction -> delayed retrieval -> labeling -> gating decision

paper_title: Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback
paper_authors: Kaixuan Ji, Zixiang Chen, Wenting Zhao, Cheng Qian, Heng Wang
